hunks.baseline: Even as night deepened, the lights of Xining stayed bright.
hunks.sol: Even as night deepened, the lights of Xining stayed lit.

hunks.baseline: The countless people still out in the streets shared their joy without holding back, and the city’s leaders provided them with liquor and meat.
hunks.sol: The countless people still in the streets shared their joy freely, and the city’s leaders provided liquor and meat for them.

hunks.baseline: They hoped the little sparks of hope nestled in those people’s hearts would burn a little longer—and a little brighter.
hunks.sol: They hoped the small sparks of hope in those people’s hearts would burn a little longer—and a little brighter.

hunks.baseline: But even as laughter from outside slipped through the cracks around the windows, the mood inside the pavilion remained heavy.
hunks.sol: But while laughter still slipped through the gaps around the windows, the mood inside the pavilion was heavy.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang broke the silence without warning, clicking his tongue as he continued.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang broke the silence with a click of his tongue.

hunks.baseline: It was the sort of thing only Jeok Cheongang could say. But because he was Jeok Cheongang, no one could bring themselves to be the first to take the plunge.
hunks.sol: Only Jeok Cheongang could say something like that. But with Jeok Cheongang on the receiving end, no one dared be the first to answer.

hunks.baseline: The leaders trailed off, exchanging glances. Just then, I spoke up from where I stood by the window.
hunks.sol: The leaders trailed off and exchanged glances. That was when I spoke up from beside the window.

hunks.baseline: “If it’s difficult to say right now, let’s start with the current situation in the city.”
hunks.sol: “If it’s hard to say right now, let’s start with the situation inside the city.”

hunks.baseline: The martial world might call the Fire Gate Clan a bunch of bastards, but it was only natural that a young Disciple felt easier to approach than a notorious old monster with a foul temper.
hunks.sol: The martial world might spell it *Fire Gate Clan* and pronounce it *bunch of bastards*, but of course a young Disciple was easier to approach than an old monster notorious for his foul temper.

hunks.baseline: I quietly smacked my lips, then turned to the speaker.
hunks.sol: I pressed my lips together, then asked the speaker, “Understood. And your name?”

hunks.baseline: “Understood. And may I ask your name?”
“I’m Cheok Mo, Sect Leader of Qinghai’s Gonghwa Sect. I don’t know if you’ve heard of us.”
hunks.sol: “Cheok Mo, Sect Leader of Qinghai’s Gonghwa Sect. I don’t know if you’ve heard of us.”

hunks.baseline: I might have known Gonghwachun, but I hadn’t memorized the names of the dozens of martial sects in Qinghai Province.
hunks.sol: I knew of Gonghwachun,[^1] but I hadn’t memorized the dozens of martial sects in Qinghai Province. And his first answer had already made it clear I wasn’t likely to remember him, either.

hunks.baseline: And his very first answer made it clear that I wasn’t likely to remember him in the future, either.
“You’re free to leave. If all you’re going to do is state the obvious, that is.”
hunks.sol: “You’re free to leave if you’re going to keep stating the obvious.”

hunks.baseline: “And when did we get so familiar? What do you think, sir?”
hunks.sol: “And since when are we on such familiar terms? What do you think, sir?”

hunks.baseline: I added the question and turned my gaze to a middle-aged official dressed in silk robes. He swallowed nervously before answering.
hunks.sol: I turned to a middle-aged official dressed in silk robes. He swallowed before answering.

hunks.baseline: “That’s a strange answer. I don’t think I asked whether you’d contradict me.”
hunks.sol: “Strange answer. I don’t recall asking whether you’d contradict me.”

hunks.baseline: “Sure. Anyway, I’ve been standing here for a while, and my legs are getting a bit tired. Is there an open seat?”
hunks.sol: “Sure. Anyway, I’ve been standing for a while, and my legs are getting tired. Is there an open seat?”

hunks.baseline: I could have stood there for days without a problem, and there were plenty of open seats. But the middle-aged official sprang from his chair.
hunks.sol: I could have stood there for days without a problem, and I didn’t even have to turn my head to see an empty chair. But the official sprang from his seat.

hunks.baseline: “There’s a seat right here!”
hunks.sol: “There’s one right here!”

hunks.baseline: “What do you mean, what should you do? Are you trying to set me up to get cursed out? Make it look like some kid who hasn’t even dried the blood from his head is throwing his rank around to bully his elders?”
hunks.sol: “What do you mean, you don’t know? Are you trying to get me cursed out? Make it look like some wet-behind-the-ears kid is throwing his rank around to bully an elder?”

hunks.baseline: The official’s eyes darted back and forth as he cautiously started to lower himself into the chair. I muttered as if to myself:
hunks.sol: The official’s eyes darted back and forth as he cautiously lowered himself toward the chair. I muttered as if to myself.

hunks.baseline: “He’s actually sitting. Doesn’t know how to read the room.”
hunks.sol: “He’s actually going to sit. Can’t read the room at all.”

hunks.baseline: “Hm? What is it?”
hunks.sol: “Hm? What?”

hunks.baseline: “I mean, what you just said…”
hunks.sol: “What you just said…”

hunks.baseline: “Oh, did you hear me?”
hunks.sol: “Oh, did you hear that?”

hunks.baseline: “I was just talking to myself. Go ahead and sit.”
hunks.sol: “I was only talking to myself. Go ahead and sit.”

hunks.baseline: “Why do I have to keep telling you? Sit down.”
hunks.sol: “Why do you keep making me repeat myself? Sit down.”

hunks.baseline: If he’d been completely clueless, he might have eased himself into the chair anyway. But the middle-aged official before me could only stare at me with eyes that seemed to shake, unable to move either way.
hunks.sol: A truly clueless man might have eased himself into the chair. This official could only stare at me, his eyes trembling, unable to sit or stand.

hunks.baseline: Then again, he must have been good at reading the room to have landed such an important post as City Lord at a relatively young age.
hunks.sol: Then again, he must have known how to read people to land a post as important as City Lord while still relatively young.

hunks.baseline: *And that same instinct must’ve helped him skim plenty of things off the top over the years.*
hunks.sol: *That same instinct must’ve helped him siphon off plenty over the years.*

hunks.baseline: Leaving the City Lord of Qinghai sweating through an imaginary squat, I glanced to my side. Jeong Hogun was smiling with a crooked twist to his lips.
hunks.sol: Leaving the City Lord of Qinghai sweating in a half-squat, I glanced aside. Jeong Hogun was smiling crookedly.

hunks.baseline: I didn’t have a hobby of bullying old men, but what I’d heard from him on the way to Xining had thoroughly washed away any guilt I might have felt.
hunks.sol: I didn’t make a habit of bullying my elders, but what Jeong Hogun had told me on the way to Xining had washed away any guilt I might have felt.

hunks.baseline: The Embroidered Uniform Guard—the imperial family’s foremost military force, with intelligence capabilities comparable to the East Depot—had obtained the information long ago. There was no room for doubt.
hunks.sol: The Embroidered Uniform Guard was the imperial family’s foremost military force, with intelligence capabilities to rival the East Depot. It had gathered the evidence long ago. There was no reason to doubt it.

hunks.baseline: More important, though, was the state of affairs his negligence had brought about.
hunks.sol: More important, though, was what the City Lord’s negligence had done to us now.

hunks.baseline: “I heard somewhere that the city’s food stores aren’t all that plentiful. What do you have to say about that, City Lord?”
hunks.sol: “I heard the city’s food stores are running low. What do you have to say about that, City Lord?”

hunks.baseline: “Just the numbers. No lies.”
hunks.sol: “Just the number. No lies.”

hunks.baseline: “W-We had far too many commoners flood the city in a short time…”
hunks.sol: “W-We’ve had so many people flood into the city in such a short time…”

hunks.baseline: “That’s a long tongue you’ve got. Want me to shorten it?”
hunks.sol: “You’ve got a long tongue. Want me to shorten it?”

hunks.baseline: The City Lord of Qinghai blurted out his answer, then added in an uncertain voice:
hunks.sol: He blurted out the answer, then added uncertainly, “…Probably.”

hunks.baseline: “…Probably.”
Jeong Hogun stepped forward at my call. The City Lord squeezed his eyes shut and cried out:
hunks.sol: Jeong Hogun strode forward at my call. The City Lord squeezed his eyes shut and cried out.

hunks.baseline: “F-Fifteen days! The food we have in storage will last that long at most!”
hunks.sol: “F-Fifteen days! The food we have in storage will last fifteen days at most!”

hunks.baseline: “Fifteen days. Are you sure about that this time?”
hunks.sol: “Fifteen days. Are you sure this time?”

hunks.baseline: “I-I stake my life on it!”
hunks.sol: “I stake my life on it!”

hunks.baseline: Men with plenty to lose never gamble with their lives.
hunks.sol: Men with plenty to lose didn’t gamble with their lives. That made his answer convincing—and infuriating.

hunks.baseline: And in that sense, the City Lord’s answer rang with a deep sincerity—and made me furious.

hunks.baseline: Qinghai was a border province. It was only natural that it would have more military provisions stored away than the Central Plains, in case of an invasion.
hunks.sol: Qinghai was a border province. It should have had more military provisions stockpiled than the Central Plains as a matter of course, in case of an invasion.

hunks.baseline: And yet there was only enough food for fifteen more days…
hunks.sol: And yet there was only enough food for fifteen more days.

hunks.baseline: *He’s really been eating well.*
hunks.sol: *He really helped himself.*

hunks.baseline: I sighed and looked at the City Lord. Sweat poured down his face from his impromptu leg workout, and he looked terrified.
hunks.sol: I sighed and looked at the City Lord. Sweat streamed down his terrified face from his impromptu leg workout.

hunks.baseline: “Why are you so scared? Anyone would think I was trying to kill you. Am I?”
hunks.sol: “Why are you so scared? Anyone would think I was trying to kill you. Wouldn’t they?”

hunks.baseline: I smiled gently at the City Lord, whose face had brightened at once, and added:

hunks.baseline: “At least not right now.”
hunks.sol: His face brightened at once. I added gently, “At least not right now.”

hunks.baseline: “Why are you asking me to repeat myself? You heard me.”
hunks.sol: “Why ask me to repeat it? You heard me.”

hunks.baseline: At that moment, three or four Embroidered Uniform Guards came striding up behind the City Lord and surrounded him.
hunks.sol: Three or four Embroidered Uniform Guards strode up behind him and surrounded him.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: “Who says we can’t?”
hunks.sol: “Who says I can’t?”

hunks.baseline: It was a terrible turn of events for the City Lord, but as the man who’d saved the imperial family and been personally appointed a marquis by the Son of Heaven, I had more than enough authority and grounds to do this.
hunks.sol: It was a terrible turn of events for the City Lord. But I had saved the imperial family, and the Son of Heaven had personally appointed me a marquis. I had more than enough authority and grounds to do this.

hunks.baseline: And his fate had been all but decided before I even set foot in Xining.
hunks.sol: Besides, his fate had been all but decided before I set foot in Xining.

hunks.baseline: “Send him off at sunrise. And don’t forget to give him some company on the way. He might get lonely.”
hunks.sol: “Send him off at sunrise. And don’t forget to give him some company for the journey. He might get lonely.”

hunks.baseline: Jeong Hogun answered more firmly than ever, then gestured. At his signal, the other Embroidered Uniform Guards waiting nearby swiftly carried out their orders.
hunks.sol: Jeong Hogun’s answer was firmer than ever. At his gesture, the other Embroidered Uniform Guards waiting nearby swiftly carried out their orders.

hunks.baseline: “These are the Marquis of Shangshan’s orders. Come along quietly if you want to see tomorrow’s sunrise.”
hunks.sol: “These are the Marquis of Shangshan’s strict orders. Come quietly if you want to see tomorrow’s sunrise.”

hunks.baseline: It happened in the blink of an eye.
hunks.sol: It happened in an instant.

hunks.baseline: Generals in ornate armor and officials in robes as stiff as their necks, were dragged out one after another, their faces pale.
hunks.sol: Generals in ornate armor and officials in robes as stiff as their necks were dragged out one after another, their faces pale.

hunks.baseline: There wasn’t the slightest resistance throughout the whole process.
No—that wasn’t quite right. They hadn’t even dared to try.
hunks.sol: Not one of them resisted. No—they didn’t even dare try.

hunks.baseline: The presence of Supreme Peak masters who could shake the world had something to do with it. But the moment they opposed the imperial Embroidered Uniform Guard, their entire families could be branded traitors.
hunks.sol: The presence of Supreme Peak masters who could shake the world played a part. But if they opposed the imperial Embroidered Uniform Guard, their entire families could be branded traitors.

hunks.baseline: Beheaded as corrupt officials in league with the City Lord of Qinghai, or branded traitors and wiped out along with their families: faced with those two choices of death, they had only one option.
hunks.sol: Beheaded as corrupt officials in league with the City Lord, or branded traitors and wiped out along with their families. Faced with that choice, they could do only one thing.

hunks.baseline: And despair without end.
hunks.sol: And despair.

hunks.baseline: But unlike those men, dragged away to wail as if everything were over, the people would grow more united and rejoice now that the tumor had been removed.
hunks.sol: Unlike the men dragged out wailing as though everything was over, the people would rejoice and draw closer together once this tumor was removed.

hunks.baseline: And along with that—
hunks.sol: And there was something else.

hunks.baseline: Those dozen or so seats, emptied in an instant, meant the presence of someone had filled the void they left behind.
hunks.sol: The dozen or so seats emptied in an instant. Yet the void they left was filled by the presence of the man who had emptied them.

hunks.baseline: The presence of Jin Taekyung, the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.
hunks.sol: Jin Taekyung, the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.

hunks.baseline: Suffocating silence weighed down on the pavilion.
hunks.sol: Suffocating silence weighed on the pavilion.

hunks.baseline: Those close to me were smiling quietly, but the faces and eyes of those who didn’t know me had sunk into darkness as they looked at one another.
hunks.sol: Those close to me smiled without a sound. Those who didn’t know me exchanged dark looks.

hunks.baseline: Their backs, now sitting straight. Their fingers, tapping the table slowly, but with growing impatience.
hunks.sol: Backs that had once been relaxed were now rigidly straight. Fingers tapped the table slowly, anxiously.

hunks.baseline: Some of them might have looked down on me in their hearts, or tried to diminish me.
Rumors always grew out of proportion.
And in an unsettled age like this, heroes were sometimes made because people needed them.
hunks.sol: Perhaps some of them had dismissed me in private, or tried to diminish what I’d done. Rumors always grew in the telling. And in troubled times like these, people sometimes made heroes because they needed them.

hunks.baseline: There had always been people like that, no matter the time or place. And the outcome had always been the same.
hunks.sol: There had always been people like that, everywhere. The result had always been the same.

hunks.baseline: There had also always been those who watched everything in silence, their expressions impossible to read.
Like the young Daoist who now looked straight at me, unlike the few who were avoiding my gaze.
hunks.sol: And there had always been people who watched in silence, giving nothing away. Like the young Daoist who looked straight at me now while a few others avoided my gaze.

hunks.baseline: “Rumors are ultimately made through the eyes and ears of those who hear them, so I never put much stock in them, as usual.”
hunks.sol: “Rumors are made from what people see and hear. As usual, I didn’t put much stock in them.”

hunks.baseline: His Daoist robes were neat, without a single wrinkle, and his eyes had a depth impossible to fathom.
hunks.sol: His Daoist robes were neat, without a single wrinkle, and I couldn’t begin to read the depths of his eyes.

hunks.baseline: “But meeting you in person has shown me again that I was right.”
hunks.sol: “But now that I’ve met you, fellow Daoist, I see once again that I was right.”

hunks.baseline: His voice was calm and unruffled, just like his neatly arranged appearance.
hunks.sol: His voice was as calm and composed as his appearance.

hunks.baseline: “It seems rumors aren’t very reliable. Sometimes they fall short—and sometimes… they exceed every expectation.”
hunks.sol: “Rumors can’t be trusted. Sometimes the truth falls short of them. Other times… it far surpasses them.”

hunks.baseline: The young Daoist rose from his seat, clasped his hands toward me in greeting, and spoke.
hunks.sol: The young Daoist rose, clasped his hands in greeting, and spoke.
[^1]: Gonghwachun is a Korean Chinese restaurant whose name sounds like Gonghwa Sect.
